newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Park Seuk-tae, a former executive director of the Korea First Bank who was involved in the Hanbo Group loan scandal, hanged himself at his home on Monday.
- Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo was excused by the judge 10 minutes after the trial opened due to his poor health.
- Prosecutors said they would seek an arrest warrant today for Park Tae-joong, an associate of the president's son, on charges of bribery, embezzlement and tax evasion.
- Creditor banks of the Jinro Group agreed at a meeting of creditors to provide 80.4 billion won in emergency funds to help the debt-ridden conglomerate head off an imminent liquidity crisis.
- A top ruling party offical said President Kim Young-sam would not endorse a candidate during the ruling party's presidential nomination convention in order to keep the competition fair.
- North Korea called for South Korea's help to boost agricultural productivity in its southwestern rice belt on the condition it could repay the South with farm products, officials said Monday.
- North Korea's Red Cross on Monday rejected a proposal by its South Korean counterpart for a border meeting this week to discuss food aid to help avert famine in the North.
